name: add_tests_kotlin_classifier
description: Asks the model to write JUnit tests for a Kotlin classifier; mutation-checked
prompts: PasswordStrength.classify in src/main/kotlin/com/optarena/app/PasswordStrength.kt (already correct, do not modify it) implements: shorter than 8 characters -> "weak"; at least 8 but either shorter than 12 or containing no digit -> "medium"; otherwise (12+ characters AND at least one digit) -> "strong". Write JUnit 5 tests for it at exactly src/test/kotlin/com/optarena/app/PasswordStrengthTest.kt (package com.optarena.app, class PasswordStrengthTest), with at least 3 separate @Test functions covering: a short password classified weak; a medium-length password classified medium; a 12+-character password WITHOUT a digit classified medium; and a 12+-character password with a digit classified strong. Use assertEquals from org.junit.jupiter.api.Assertions.

test_setup_files.mutation_check.py:
import shutil
import subprocess
from pathlib import Path

IMPL = Path("src/main/kotlin/com/optarena/app/PasswordStrength.kt")
TEST_CMD = "mvn -o -q test -Dtest=PasswordStrengthTest"
MUTANTS = [[["            len < 8 -> \"weak\"", "            len < 8 -> \"medium\""]], [["            len < 12 || !hasDigit -> \"medium\"", "            len < 12 || !hasDigit -> \"strong\""]]]

def run_tests():
    shutil.rmtree("target/classes", ignore_errors=True)
    return subprocess.run(TEST_CMD, shell=True).returncode

src = IMPL.read_text(encoding="utf-8")
for group in MUTANTS:
    for old, _new in group:
        assert src.count(old) == 1, (
            f"protected implementation file {IMPL} was modified - the task said not to change it "
            f"(anchor not found exactly once: {old!r})")

rc = run_tests()
assert rc == 0, f"model tests FAILED against the correct implementation (exit {rc})"

try:
    for i, group in enumerate(MUTANTS, 1):
        mutated = src
        for old, new in group:
            mutated = mutated.replace(old, new)
        IMPL.write_text(mutated, encoding="utf-8")
        rc = run_tests()
        assert rc != 0, (
            f"mutation {i} SURVIVED: the tests still pass against a deliberately broken "
            f"implementation, so they do not actually verify the required behavior")
finally:
    IMPL.write_text(src, encoding="utf-8")

print("PASS (tests pass on correct impl and kill all {n} mutants)".format(n=len(MUTANTS)))
